mainTopic: Selling a wine cellar (the role of 'this' and of מקפה) and the ברכה over lower-quality wine
overview: רב זביד's ברייתא says that when a seller points to 'this' cellar, the buyer accepts up to ten souring barrels per hundred, and that this is the משנה's case. So the גמרא now reads the משנה as a 'this' case too. That clashes with the first ברייתא, where 'this' cellar lets the seller give shop-quality wine. The גמרא resolves it: רב זביד's ברייתא is where the buyer said the wine is for a cooked dish (מקפה), and the first ברייתא is where he did not. It then lists the rules for three cases. רב אחא and רבינא argue about the fourth case, 'a' cellar with no mention of מקפה. Each side draws on a different ברייתא and answers the challenge from the other one. The גמרא then turns to the ברכה over shop wine. רב יהודה says it gets בורא פרי הגפן, and רב זביד limits a ברייתא that gives שהכל to cheap grape-seed wine. אביי asks רב יוסף whether he follows רב יהודה or רב חסדא, and רב יוסף says he knows a ברייתא, which is quoted on the next amud.

steps.title: רב זביד's ברייתא ties its case to the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of רב זביד's ברייתא says that its case, where the seller pointed to 'this' wine and the buyer accepts some souring barrels, is the very case the משנה was teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the 'storeroom' that the Sages taught in our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from רב זביד's ברייתא. Its last line says that the case it just described is the case of the cellar in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא had suggested that the משנה (buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred) was about a sale where the seller did not name a specific cellar. רב זביד's ברייתא is a 'this' case, and it ends by saying that this is the משנה's case. That works against the earlier suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Storeroom; here, the wine cellar being sold
That the Sages taught
In our משנה

phrases.english: And this is the storeroom
that the Sages taught in our משנה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא quoted just before this point, which challenges the earlier reading of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's case is one where the seller said 'this' cellar
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב זביד's ברייתא, which explicitly identifies its 'this' case with the משנה

steps.title: The משנה is also about 'this' cellar
steps.stepSummary: Because of רב זביד's ברייתא, the גמרא gives up its earlier reading. The משנה too is a case where the seller said 'this' cellar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, our משנה is also a case where he said to him 'this' cellar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs down from its earlier reading. It now says the משנה is also a case where the seller pointed to a specific cellar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals a retreat: the earlier way of reading the משנה is dropped. Now the משנה and רב זביד's ברייתא match: a 'this' cellar, where the buyer accepts up to ten souring barrels per hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals dropping an earlier idea
Our משנה
Also
'This', meaning the seller pointed to a specific cellar

phrases.english: Rather, our משנה also
is where he said to him 'this'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of רב זביד's ברייתא and changes how the משנה is read.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's rule (accept ten souring barrels per hundred) applies when the seller said 'this' cellar.

steps.title: Two ברייתות about 'this' cellar now clash
steps.stepSummary: Now there is a contradiction. The first ברייתא says 'this' cellar means the seller may give shop-quality wine. רב זביד's ברייתא says 'this' cellar means the wine must be good, with the buyer accepting up to ten souring barrels per hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: a 'this' case against a 'this' case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a new problem caused by the last step. Two ברייתות talk about the same words, 'this' cellar, but give opposite rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first ברייתא, saying 'this' cellar lets the seller give shop-quality wine. In רב זביד's ברייתא, saying 'this' means he must give good wine, and the buyer accepts only up to ten souring barrels per hundred. The same wording cannot lead to both results unless the cases differ.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difficulty
'This' against 'this', meaning one 'this' case against another

steps.confusionAlert: Both sources use the same word, 'this'. The clash is not about whether a specific cellar was named. It is about what rule follows once it was named.

phrases.english: It is difficult: 'this' against 'this'!
phrases.notes: The first 'this' is the first ברייתא, where shop-quality wine is enough. The second is רב זביד's, where the wine must be good apart from up to ten souring barrels per hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The new reading in step 2 creates a contradiction between the two ברייתות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות that rule on a 'this' cellar sale
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case, 'this' cellar, gets different rules: shop-quality wine in the first ברייתא, and good wine with up to ten souring barrels per hundred in רב זביד's ברייתא.

steps.title: It depends on whether the buyer said it was for cooking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two ברייתות are different cases. In רב זביד's ברייתא the buyer said he wants the wine for a cooked dish (מקפה). In the first ברייתא he did not say that.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is where he told him it is for a cooked dish, and that one is where he did not tell him it is for a cooked dish. רב זביד's ברייתא is where he told him it is for a cooked dish. The other ברייתא is where he did not tell him it is for a cooked dish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the clash by splitting the cases. It depends on whether the buyer said he wants the wine for a cooked dish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד's ruling, good wine with up to ten souring barrels per hundred, is for a buyer who said the wine is for a מקפה, a cooked dish. The first ברייתא's ruling, where shop-quality wine is enough, is for a buyer who said nothing about cooking. Since the buyer's stated purpose is different, the rules no longer contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; introduces an answer
This one ... that one; splitting two cases
A cooked dish that wine is used in

steps.whatToRemember: In a 'this' cellar sale, if the buyer said the wine is for a cooked dish (מקפה), the wine must be good, but he accepts up to ten souring barrels per hundred, as in רב זביד's ברייתא and the משנה. If he did not say that, the seller may give shop-quality wine, as in the first ברייתא.
steps.confusionAlert: Read the last line carefully. רב זביד's ברייתא, the one where some souring is accepted, is the case where the buyer DID say 'for a cooked dish'.

phrases.english: It is not difficult;
this one is where he told him 'for a cooked dish',
phrases.notes: The buyer told the seller he wants the wine for cooking a dish.

phrases.english: that one is where he did not tell him 'for a cooked dish'.
The one of רב זביד is where he told him 'for a cooked dish',
the ברייתא is where he did not tell him 'for a cooked dish'.
phrases.notes: 'The ברייתא' means the first ברייתא, the one that allows shop-quality wine for 'this' cellar.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה הָא דְּלָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source is about a different case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to describe the same 'this' cellar sale and give opposite rules.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ in whether the buyer said the wine was for a cooked dish. רב זביד's ברייתא is where he did; the first ברייתא is where he did not.
steps.whyThisMatters: What the buyer says he needs the goods for can change what quality the seller has to deliver.

steps.title: Summary of the three wine-cellar cases
steps.stepSummary: Using the answer from the last step, the גמרא lists the rule for three cases: 'a' cellar with מקפה, 'this' cellar with מקפה, and 'this' cellar without מקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the rules are: If the seller said 'a wine cellar' and the buyer said it is for a cooked dish, the seller must give wine that is all good. If the seller said 'this wine cellar' and the buyer said it is for a cooked dish, the seller gives good wine, but the buyer accepts ten souring barrels in every hundred. If the seller said 'this wine cellar' and the buyer did not mention a cooked dish, the seller may give wine of the kind sold in a shop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls everything together into one clear list of rules for selling a wine cellar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things set the rule. Saying 'this' cellar makes the buyer more willing to take what is there, and saying 'for מקפה' makes the buyer more demanding. The strictest case for the seller is 'a' cellar plus מקפה, where all the wine must be good. The easiest case for him is 'this' cellar with no מקפה, where shop-quality wine is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore. It introduces a summary or conclusion.
A wine cellar, a store of wine barrels.
A cooked dish. The buyer wants the wine to cook with, so he needs it in good condition.
Barrels that are starting to turn sour.
Wine sold in a shop, meaning ordinary wine that is beginning to sour and has to be used quickly.

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases are settled. 'A' cellar plus מקפה means all good. 'This' cellar plus מקפה means good, but ten souring barrels per hundred are accepted. 'This' cellar with no מקפה means shop-quality wine.
steps.confusionAlert: In the middle case, 'all good' and 'accepts ten souring barrels' are not a contradiction. The seller must give good wine, but up to ten barrels per hundred may be souring.

phrases.english: Therefore,
if he said "a wine cellar," and the buyer told him "for a cooked dish":
he gives him wine that is all good.

phrases.aramaic: ״מַרְתֵּף זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן״ וְאָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה –
phrases.english: If he said "this wine cellar," and the buyer told him "for a cooked dish":
he gives him wine that is all good,
but the buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred.

phrases.aramaic: ״מַרְתֵּף זֶה שֶׁל יַיִן״ וְלָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה –
phrases.english: If he said "this wine cellar," and the buyer did not tell him "for a cooked dish":
he gives him wine of the kind sold in a shop.
phrases.notes: Shop wine is wine that is starting to turn, so the shopkeeper sells it off quickly, cup by cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer in step 4 (the two ברייתות differ over מקפה) into a full set of rules.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The rule depends on whether the seller said 'this' and whether the buyer said 'for מקפה'. Three of the four possible cases are now settled.

steps.title: What about 'a' cellar without mentioning a cooked dish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the fourth case, which the summary left out: the seller said 'a' cellar and the buyer did not mention מקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if the seller said 'a wine cellar' and the buyer did not say it was for a cooked dish, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that one case is missing from the list and asks about it. This sets up the disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two factors, so there are four possible cases, and only three were settled. In this case one factor points toward 'all good' (the seller did not say 'this'), and the other points toward leniency (the buyer did not say מקפה). So it is not clear which way the rule goes.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the חכמים. It introduces an open question.
What is the rule?

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:

phrases.aramaic: ״מַרְתֵּף שֶׁל יַיִן״ וְלָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה, מַאי?
phrases.english: If he said "a wine cellar," and the buyer did not tell him "for a cooked dish," what is the rule?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks out the one combination the summary in step 5 did not cover.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a buyer of 'a' wine cellar who did not mention מקפה must accept ten souring barrels per hundred.

steps.title: רב אחא and רבינא disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים argue about the question. One says the buyer accepts souring barrels, and the other says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא and רבינא disagree about this. One says the buyer accepts the souring barrels. The other says he does not accept them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a disagreement. We are not told which אמורא holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מקבל' means the buyer must take ten souring barrels per hundred, as in the 'this' cellar plus מקפה case. 'לא מקבל' means the seller must give all good wine, with no souring barrels at all.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree.
One said. Used when we do not know which of the two holds which view.
He accepts, meaning the buyer must take the souring barrels.

phrases.english: Rav Acha and Ravina disagree about it;
one says: he accepts,
phrases.notes: He means the buyer has to take ten souring barrels in every hundred.

phrases.english: and one says: he does not accept.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 6 with two opposite views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a disagreement. One view says the buyer accepts ten souring barrels per hundred, and the other says he gets all good wine.

steps.title: The 'accepts' view reads it from רב זביד's ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The view that the buyer accepts souring barrels learns it by reading closely in רב זביד's ברייתא, which we explained as a case where the buyer said מקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'he accepts' reads it out of רב זביד's ברייתא. It teaches: 'I am selling you a wine cellar' means he gives wine that is all good. And we explained that case as one where the buyer said 'for a cooked dish.' So the only reason the wine must be all good is that he said 'for a cooked dish.' If he did not say that, the buyer accepts souring barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the first view gets its idea. It reads closely in רב זביד's ברייתא and draws out what the ברייתא implies without saying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we said רב זביד's ברייתא is talking about a buyer who said מקפה. So its ruling that 'a' cellar means all good wine depends on the mention of מקפה. Take away מקפה, and the buyer must accept some souring barrels.

keyTerms.meaning: He reads closely, drawing out something the text implies without saying it.
We explained it as a specific case.
'The reason is... but otherwise.' This is the pattern for drawing a conclusion from what the text does not say.

phrases.english: The one who says "he accepts":
reads it closely from the ברייתא of Rav Zevid, which teaches:
"I am selling you a wine cellar":
he gives him wine that is all good,
and we explained it as a case where the buyer told him "for a cooked dish";
phrases.notes: This points back to the answer in step 4.

phrases.english: the reason is that he told him "for a cooked dish,"

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה – מְקַבֵּל.
phrases.english: but if he did not tell him "for a cooked dish," he accepts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מְקַבֵּל דָּיֵיק מִדְּרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the first view in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a buyer of 'a' cellar who did not mention מקפה must accept souring barrels.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A close reading of רב זביד's ברייתא, which was explained as a case where the buyer said מקפה.

steps.title: The 'does not accept' view reads it from the first ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The view that the buyer does not accept souring barrels reads it from the first ברייתא, which says 'a' cellar means all good wine, and which we explained as a case where the buyer did not say מקפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'he does not accept' reads it out of the first ברייתא. It teaches: 'I am selling you a wine cellar' means he gives wine that is all good. And we explained that ברייתא as a case where the buyer did not say 'for a cooked dish.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the source for the second view. Here the ברייתא states the rule openly, for exactly the case being asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 we said the first ברייתא is talking about a buyer who did not say מקפה. Its 'a' cellar case therefore matches our question exactly, and it rules that all the wine must be good. So in this case the buyer does not have to take any souring barrels.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה. Here it means the first ברייתא of the סוגיא.
I am selling you. These are the seller's words in the case.

steps.whatToRemember: Each אמורא relies on a different ברייתא. 'Accepts' learns it from what רב זביד's ברייתא implies, and 'does not accept' learns it from what the first ברייתא says outright.

phrases.english: And the one who says "he does not accept":
reads it closely from the ברייתא, which teaches:
phrases.notes: This is the first ברייתא from earlier in the סוגיא, not רב זביד's.

phrases.english: "I am selling you a wine cellar":
he gives him wine that is all good,
and we explained it as a case where he did not tell him "for a cooked dish."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא מְקַבֵּל דָּיֵיק מִבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the second view in step 7, set side by side with step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The view that a buyer of 'a' cellar who did not mention מקפה gets all good wine and accepts no souring barrels.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first ברייתא, explained as a case where the buyer did not say מקפה, which rules that all the wine must be good.

steps.title: The first ברייתא challenges the view that the buyer accepts
steps.stepSummary: The view that learns from רב זביד's ברייתא (the buyer accepts souring barrels) is challenged by the first ברייתא, which says 'a' cellar means all good wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who learns his view from רב זביד's ברייתא, the first ברייתא is a problem!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first opinion. If a buyer who did not say מקפה must accept souring barrels, how does that fit the first ברייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we explained the first ברייתא as a case where the buyer did not say מקפה. It rules that 'a' cellar means all good wine, so the buyer does not have to accept souring barrels. That is the opposite of what this opinion holds.

keyTerms.meaning: who reads closely and draws an inference
it is a difficulty, a problem

phrases.english: And according to the one who infers from Rav Zevid's [ברייתא],
phrases.notes: This is the opinion from Step 8: the buyer accepts souring barrels if he didn't mention מקפה.

phrases.english: the [first] ברייתא is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּדָיֵיק מִדְּרַב זְבִיד, קַשְׁיָא בָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the second opinion's proof from Step 9 into a challenge against the first opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that a buyer who did not mention מקפה accepts souring barrels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first ברייתא, set in a case without מקפה, gives all good wine for 'a' cellar. That contradicts this opinion.

steps.title: The first ברייתא is missing words
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion answers that the first ברייתא is missing words. Its 'all good wine' ruling applies only when the buyer said מקפה. Without מקפה, he accepts souring barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it teaches: When is this ruling said? When the buyer told him the wine was for cooking. If he did not say it was for cooking, he accepts souring barrels. And if the seller said 'this cellar of wine' and the buyer did not say it was for cooking, the seller may give him wine like that sold in the shop.
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion fixes the problem by saying the first ברייתא left out some words. Once we fill them in, the ברייתא agrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing words filled in, the ruling 'a cellar means all good wine' now applies only when the buyer said מקפה. In our fourth case, where the buyer did not say מקפה, the ברייתא now says he must accept souring barrels, just as this opinion holds. The last line adds that for 'this' cellar without מקפה, the seller may hand over shop-quality wine.

keyTerms.meaning: it is missing words; something must be filled in
in what case is this said?
he accepts (the souring barrels)
wine sold in the shop, of lower quality that is starting to sour

steps.confusionAlert: The words after 'this is what it teaches' are not a new ברייתא. They are the same first ברייתא with the missing pieces filled in.

phrases.english: It is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: 'These words' means the ברייתא's ruling that 'a' cellar must be all good wine.

phrases.english: Where he said to him, "for cooking";

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה – מְקַבֵּל.
phrases.english: but if he did not say to him "for cooking," he accepts.
And "this cellar of wine"
and he did not say to him "for cooking"
he gives him wine that is sold in the shop.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ברייתא gives all good wine for 'a' cellar even when the buyer did not say מקפה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 'all good wine' ruling applies only when the buyer said מקפה. Without it, the buyer accepts souring barrels.

steps.title: רב זביד's ברייתא challenges the view that the buyer does not accept
steps.stepSummary: The view that learns from the first ברייתא is challenged by רב זביד's ברייתא. We explained that ברייתא as a case with מקפה, which suggests that without מקפה the buyer accepts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who learns his view from the first ברייתא, רב זביד's ברייתא is a problem. We explained it as a case where the buyer said 'for cooking.' That suggests that if he did not say it, he accepts souring barrels!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the second opinion with the source the first opinion relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב זביד's ברייתא needed the words 'for cooking' to free the buyer from souring barrels, it sounds like the buyer would have to accept them if he had not said it. That goes against the second opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: that we set up the case as, that we explained it as

phrases.english: And according to the one who infers from the [first] ברייתא,
Rav Zevid's [ברייתא] is difficult,
since we explained it as where he said to him "for cooking,"

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה – מְקַבֵּל!
phrases.english: which implies that if he did not say to him "for cooking," he accepts!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּדָיֵיק מִבָּרַיְיתָא, קַשְׁיָא דְּרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors Step 10, this time challenging the other opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that a buyer who did not mention מקפה does not accept souring barrels
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setting רב זביד's ברייתא in a case with מקפה implies that without מקפה the buyer accepts souring barrels.

steps.title: מקפה was added only to settle the 'this' cellar contradiction
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion answers that even without מקפה the buyer does not accept. רב זביד's ברייתא was set in a case with מקפה only to settle the contradiction between the two ברייתות about 'this' cellar.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true even if he did not say 'for cooking': he does not accept souring barrels. We explained רב זביד's ברייתא as a case where he said 'for cooking' only because the two ברייתות contradicted each other about 'this' cellar.
steps.whatsHappening: The second opinion explains that the words 'for cooking' were added to רב זביד's ברייתא for a different reason, so no inference about our case can be drawn from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail of מקפה was needed only for the 'this' cellar half of the ברייתא, to stop it from clashing with the first ברייתא. For the 'a' cellar half, מקפה makes no difference. So we cannot infer that without מקפה the buyer would accept souring barrels.

keyTerms.meaning: the same law applies
even though
'this' against 'this', meaning the two rulings about 'this' cellar

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions survive. The first says the first ברייתא is missing words. The second says the מקפה detail in רב זביד's ברייתא was only there to settle the 'this' cellar contradiction.

phrases.english: The same is true, that even though

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה – לָא מְקַבֵּל,
phrases.english: he did not say to him "for cooking," he does not accept,
and the fact that we explained it as where he said to him "for cooking"
is because "this" was difficult against "this."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָמַר לֵיהּ לְמִקְפָּה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining away the inference: the case detail was added for another reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Setting רב זביד's ברייתא with מקפה implies that without מקפה the buyer accepts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מקפה detail was needed only for 'this' cellar. In the 'a' cellar case the buyer never accepts souring barrels.

steps.title: Shop-quality wine gets בורא פרי הגפן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that over wine of shop quality one says בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Over wine that is sold in the shop, we say the ברכה 'בורא פרי הגפן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic, connected to the phrase 'wine sold in the shop' that just came up: which ברכה is said over it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shop wine is lower quality and is starting to sour. Still, רב יהודה says it keeps the regular wine ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: we say a ברכה
the ברכה over wine: who creates the fruit of the vine

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Wine that is sold in the shop,
we recite over it "who creates the fruit of the vine."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: יַיִן הַנִּמְכָּר בַּחֲנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the phrase 'wine sold in the shop' from Step 11 and opens a new topic about ברכות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Shop-quality wine gets the ברכה בורא פרי הגפן.

steps.title: רב חסדא on wine that has formed a film
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that for wine that has formed a film, the wine ברכה is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: For wine that has formed a film, why do I need that ברכה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a statement about wine that has formed a film as it starts to sour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He asks why one would need the wine ברכה over such wine. His point is that wine with a film is no longer treated as real wine for its ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: wine (Aramaic)
that has formed a film on top
why do I need it?

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥisda said:
Regarding wine that has formed a film, why do I need [it]?
phrases.notes: He means: why would you need to say בורא פרי הגפן over it at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: גַּבֵּי חַמְרָא דְּאַקְרֵים לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement about the ברכה over lower-quality wine, placed right after רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine that has formed a film does not need the wine ברכה בורא פרי הגפן.

steps.title: A ברייתא says spoiled foods, including wine with a film, get שהכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with a ברייתא that gives שהכל, not the special ברכה, to bread, wine, and cooked food that have started to spoil.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: A ברייתא teaches that over moldy bread, wine that formed a film, and a cooked dish that spoiled, one says שהכל נהיה בדברו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב יהודה, who said shop wine still gets בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that once food or wine has partly spoiled, it loses its special ברכה and gets only שהכל. This seems to clash with רב יהודה, because shop wine is lower quality, yet he still gives it the wine ברכה. The ברייתא also fits רב חסדא's view about wine that formed a film.

keyTerms.meaning: Became moldy
Formed a film on top, the sign that wine is starting to spoil
Whose form has changed, meaning a cooked dish that has spoiled
The general ברכה: by Whose word all things came to be

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Over bread that has become moldy,
and over wine that has formed a film,
and over a cooked dish that has spoiled,
one says "By Whose word all things came to be"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a ברייתא to attack רב יהודה's ruling from step 14. That ruling now stands next to רב חסדא's view from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's ruling that shop wine gets בורא פרי הגפן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If partly spoiled wine gets only שהכל, then lower-quality shop wine should not get בורא פרי הגפן either.

steps.title: רב יהודה agrees about cheap grape-seed wine sold on street corners
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the ברייתא is about very poor grape-seed wine, and רב יהודה agrees that it gets שהכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: רב יהודה agrees that grape-seed wine sold on street corners does not get בורא פרי הגפן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד defends רב יהודה by limiting the ברייתא to much worse wine than shop wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer splits the cases. Very poor wine made from grape seeds, sold cheaply on street corners, gets שהכל, and רב יהודה agrees. Shop wine still has the taste and look of wine, so it keeps בורא פרי הגפן.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, concedes
Cheap wine made from grape seeds or leftovers, very poor quality
On the street corners

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
Rav Yehuda concedes
regarding grape-seed wine that is sold on the street corners.
phrases.notes: He means that this wine does not get בורא פרי הגפן. That is what the ברייתא was talking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by narrowing the ברייתא's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a worse kind of wine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's ruling seemed to cover any lower-quality wine, including shop wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only very poor grape-seed wine sold on street corners gets שהכל. Shop wine keeps בורא פרי הגפן according to רב יהודה.

steps.title: אביי asks רב יוסף which view he follows
steps.stepSummary: אביי sets רב יהודה and רב חסדא side by side and asks רב יוסף which of them he holds like.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Here is רב יהודה's view and here is רב חסדא's view. Which one do you hold like?
steps.whatsHappening: With both views still standing, אביי asks his teacher רב יוסף for his own opinion. This sets up רב יוסף's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה is lenient and gives shop wine the wine ברכה. רב חסדא says wine that formed a film loses the wine ברכה. אביי wants to know which way to rule in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: This one ... and that one, setting two views side by side
Master, a respectful way to say 'you' to a teacher
In accordance with whom does he hold?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַב יְהוּדָה, הָא רַב חִסְדָּא;
phrases.english: This is the view of Rav Yehuda, and this is the view of Rav Ḥisda;
In accordance with whom does the Master hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יהודה's view is defended, אביי asks how to rule between the two views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב יוסף follows רב יהודה or רב חסדא on the ברכה for lower-quality wine

steps.title: רב יוסף answers that he knows a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף replies that he knows a ברייתא, which shows he relies on a source to decide the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: I know a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by pointing to a ברייתא instead of choosing a view by his own reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not simply name רב יהודה or רב חסדא. He says he knows a ברייתא, meaning a source from which the הלכה can be learned. The ברייתא itself is quoted on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A taught source, here a ברייתא
I know

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה gives shop wine בורא פרי הגפן. Only very poor grape-seed wine gets שהכל. רב חסדא says wine with a film loses the wine ברכה. רב יוסף answers the question of whom to follow by pointing to a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I know a baraita.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to אביי's question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף points to a ברייתא he knows as the basis for deciding between רב יהודה and רב חסדא. The ברייתא is quoted on the next amud.
